title: Internet in Dallas, TX: Providers, Fiber, Cable, 5G (2026)
description: Internet in Dallas, TX: Spectrum cable, AT&T Fiber and 5G home by ZIP code, from FCC data. See who reaches you and what to ask before signing up.
lead: Who serves Dallas, where fiber has reached, and how cable and 5G compare, by ZIP code.
short_answer: In June 2026 FCC data, Spectrum cable reaches most homes in all of Dallas's 54 ZIP codes and AT&T Fiber in 43. Verizon and T-Mobile 5G home internet reach most homes in 29 and 29. See who serves your ZIP code and what to ask before you sign up.

sections.h2: Every provider reporting service in Dallas (54 ZIP codes)

sections.body_html: Source: FCC Broadband Data Collection, June 30, 2026, matched to ZIP codes by YourBillCheck. "ZIP codes served" counts the 54 ZIP codes with a Dallas postal address where each provider reports service to at least 10% of locations, so it includes a few areas outside city limits and is a guide, not a promise for your street. Top speed is the fastest plan the provider reports in the city, and many homes cannot get it.

sections.h2: Cable, fiber or 5G: how Dallas's networks compare
sections.body_html:
Spectrum cable covers most homes in every Dallas ZIP code, and AT&T Fiber reaches most homes in 43 of the 54, so many Dallas addresses can compare a cable and a fiber plan.

Cable: Spectrum reports cable in 54 Dallas ZIP codes and covers most homes in all of them, with top speeds of 1 Gbps.

Fiber: AT&T reports fiber in 54 ZIP codes and covers most homes in 43. AT&T's own Dallas page lists plans from 300 Mbps to 1 Gig and speeds up to 5 Gbps where available, depending on address. Sonic reports fiber in 5 ZIP codes, and Frontier and Spectrum each report some fiber, so a few neighborhoods have a third wired choice.

5G home internet: Verizon reaches most homes in 29 ZIP codes and T-Mobile in 29. Speeds are lower and vary more than wired plans (T-Mobile reports up to 100 Mbps and Verizon up to 1 Gbps here). These plans are worth a look if you want no contract and a simple bill, and they are the main alternative where fiber is missing.

In 43 of 54 Dallas ZIP codes, at least one fiber network reaches most homes (75% or more of locations). In the other 11, fiber is partial or absent, so cable, 5G or a partial fiber build are the realistic choices: 75201, 75202, 75204, 75219, 75240, 75243, 75252, 75253, 75254, 75270, 75287.

Partial means your street may still have fiber while your neighbor's does not. Enter your address on the provider's site, or use our fiber checker, before assuming either way.

sections.h2: What to ask before you sign up
sections.body_html:
1. Is my exact address on fiber or cable? Providers report coverage by area, and availability differs street by street.
  2. What is the price after the promotion, and is there a price lock? Compare the price in month 13, not month 1.
  3. Is there a data allowance, installation fee or equipment charge?
  4. For 5G home internet: what speed does my address get, and is there a trial period?

Run a speed test on your current plan first, and use the low-income internet checker if you may qualify for a discount. If your bill has crept up, read why your internet bill went up and our guide to internet fees.
See every Dallas-area provider and ZIP code on our Dallas provider list, or the Texas overview. Or run the availability checker with your ZIP code.

faq: What is the main internet provider in Dallas?

Spectrum cable is the most widely available wired network, covering most homes in 54 of 54 Dallas ZIP codes in June 2026 FCC data. AT&T Fiber reports service in 54 ZIP codes and covers most homes in 43.
Yes. AT&T Fiber covers most homes in 43 of 54 Dallas ZIP codes. In 43 ZIP codes at least one fiber network reaches most homes, and in 11 fiber is partial or absent. Check your address.
Can I get 5G home internet in Dallas?
Yes. Verizon reports 5G home internet reaching most homes in 29 of 54 Dallas ZIP codes and T-Mobile in 29. Speeds vary by address, so use each provider's address check.
Is satellite internet available in Dallas?
Starlink reports service across Dallas, and HughesNet and Viasat may also report service. For most Dallas homes a wired or 5G plan is faster and cheaper, so satellite is a last resort.
sources: FCC Broadband Data Collection (June 30, 2026), Dallas ZIP codes, via YourBillCheck
